Prossiga via

An ATC instruction directing an aircraft to follow a specified route, airway, or series of waypoints.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Prossiga via?

In this glossary, Prossiga via refers to: An ATC instruction directing an aircraft to follow a specified route, airway, or series of waypoints.

How is Prossiga via used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "ATC: N789EF, prossiga via a aerovia VICTOR 12 até o ponto CHARLIE."

Why does Prossiga via matter in aviation?

Prossiga via matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Prossiga via?

Prossiga via is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Prossiga via belong to?

In this glossary, Prossiga via is grouped under Basic ATC. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

An ATC instruction directing an aircraft to follow a specified route, airway, or series of waypoints.

Operational example

ATC: N789EF, proceed via VICTOR 12 airway to CHARLIE waypoint.

Localized term

Prossiga via

Localized example

ATC: N789EF, prossiga via a aerovia VICTOR 12 até o ponto CHARLIE.
